limitations: The rule contains no event for KeyPairGenerator, AlgorithmParameterGenerator, Signature, KeyAgreement, or provider lookup.
The rule has no predicate establishing that the selected provider recognizes an allow-listed alias or OID.
The rule provides no curve-size, protocol-purpose, key-lifetime, validation, randomness, or downstream-use condition.
A static implementation may be unable to prove a dynamic string's runtime value even where the runtime membership condition is satisfied.
The rule text does not state that its finite allow-list is the complete or current Java standard-name registry.
predicates: The governed API type named by the rule is java.security.spec.ECGenParameterSpec.
The required event is c1: ECGenParameterSpec(stdName).
The sole order requirement is that c1 occurs.
The constructor argument's value at execution belongs to the exact finite string set in the CRYSL CONSTRAINTS clause.
The postcondition stated by the rule is preparedEC[this].
detector_semantics.claim: A compliant c1 constructor event establishes preparedEC[this] for the newly constructed ECGenParameterSpec object.

unknowns: The CRYSL source does not explain the security rationale for its particular allow-list or the meaning intended for preparedEC beyond the stated ENSURES predicate.
The rule does not identify a target Java release, provider set, or organizational cryptographic policy.
It is unresolved whether the detector implementation evaluates string membership exactly at runtime, symbolically, by constants only, or through another approximation.
The rule does not establish whether listed aliases and OIDs are recognized uniformly by all providers.
The rule does not connect the specification object to any later provider operation, so the actual selected curve and security-relevant use remain unresolved.

documented_behavior: ECGenParameterSpec is an immutable AlgorithmParameterSpec for identifying precomputed elliptic-curve domain parameters by a standard or predefined name.
The constructor creates the specification from stdName; the API documentation directs callers to the selected provider's documentation for supported names.
Java's standard algorithm-name specification separately lists standardized ECGenParameterSpec names.
preconditions: stdName must be non-null; the documented constructor exception is NullPointerException when it is null.
A non-null name must be supported by the provider ultimately used if the specification is later supplied to a provider operation requiring that curve.
Provider support and aliases are implementation-dependent beyond the platform's documented minimum requirements.
unknowns: The constructor documentation does not declare that every non-null name is validated or rejected at construction time.
The documentation does not make the detector's allow-list a complete list of provider-supported names.
The documentation does not state that every standardized ECGenParameterSpec name is available from every third-party provider.

non_security_violation_shapes: `ECGenParameterSpec("unrecognized-test-name")` created solely in a unit test or negative test and never supplied to a cryptographic provider.
An unallow-listed name placed in an object that is never used for parameter initialization, key generation, signing, verification, encryption, decryption, or key agreement.

An unallow-listed name that is later rejected by the provider before any key material is generated or used; this violates the detector's membership condition but does not by itself establish a security impact.
important_note: This specification observes only construction of java.security.spec.ECGenParameterSpec and applies a fixed name allow-list. Its ENSURES clause marks the resulting object as preparedEC[this] after a compliant construction, but it does not prove that a provider accepts the name, that the object initializes a key generator, that keys are generated, or that any generated key is appropriate for a particular protocol or security policy.

events.condition: At execution of the constructor call, stdName must be one of: "brainpoolP224r1", "1.3.36.3.3.2.8.1.1.5", "brainpoolP256r1", "1.3.36.3.3.2.8.1.1.7", "brainpoolP320r1", "1.3.36.3.3.2.8.1.1.9", "brainpoolP384r1", "1.3.36.3.3.2.8.1.1.11", "brainpoolP512r1", "1.3.36.3.3.2.8.1.1.13", "secp224r1", "NIST P-224", "1.3.132.0.33", "secp256r1", "NIST P-256", "X9.62 prime256v1", "1.2.840.10045.3.1.7", "secp384r1", "NIST P-384", "1.3.132.0.34", "secp521r1", "NIST P-521", or "1.3.132.0.35". This is a runtime value-membership predicate, not a requirement that the source argument be spelled as a string literal.

security_semantics.runtime_claim: At runtime, the JCA API represents a named EC parameter request. Whether it is usable depends on the provider later selected, and whether it is suitable depends on the actual cryptographic operation and deployment policy.
security_semantics.detector_claim: The detector treats construction with a name in its fixed allow-list as sufficient to label that ECGenParameterSpec object preparedEC.

compatibility: Consult the selected provider's documentation for its supported ECGenParameterSpec names and aliases.
Check the Java Security Standard Algorithm Names specification for standardized names applicable to the deployed Java release.
Verify any required interoperability profile or organizational curve policy independently of the detector allow-list.
runtime: Capture the effective stdName value at the constructor invocation.
Identify the JCA provider and JDK/runtime version used by the later cryptographic operation.
If compatibility is at issue, initialize the relevant provider service with the specification and record whether it accepts the name.
If security impact is claimed, establish that the resulting parameters are actually used for a security-relevant key-generation or cryptographic operation.
source_level: Resolve the constructed type to java.security.spec.ECGenParameterSpec rather than a same-named type from another package or framework.
Establish that the constructor call is reachable if reporting an executable finding rather than a dead-code observation.
For an asserted rule violation, establish the possible runtime value or values of stdName rather than relying solely on the source spelling of an expression.
Use the CRYSL rule source as the authority for the detector's exact finite allow-list and preparedEC postcondition.

forbidden_inferences_without_evidence: That an allow-listed name is supported by the installed or selected JCA provider.
That construction alone causes EC parameters to be generated or any key pair to be generated.
That the constructed specification is subsequently supplied to KeyPairGenerator.initialize or another cryptographic API.
That an allow-listed curve name meets the deployment's current security, compliance, interoperability, or protocol requirements.
That a name absent from the rule is unsupported by the JCA API or insecure.
That a finding identifies a particular EC signature, key-agreement, certificate, SSH, TLS, or other protocol use.
name: ECGenParameterSpecSpec
semantic_scope: For every finding of this rule, the detector observes a construction event for java.security.spec.ECGenParameterSpec and tests the constructor argument's runtime string value against the rule's fixed allow-list. It does not observe provider selection, provider support, later initialization, key generation, key use, or the surrounding protocol.
known_false_positive_shapes: A non-literal value such as `val curve = configuredCurveName(); ECGenParameterSpec(curve)` where the value at execution is an exact allow-listed string, but static analysis cannot establish that value.
`ECGenParameterSpec("SECP256R1")` where the applicable Java standard-name specification treats standard names as case-insensitive, while the CRYSL constraint spells only lowercase `"secp256r1"`.

`ECGenParameterSpec("secp256k1")` on a runtime/provider that supports it: the current Java Security Standard Algorithm Names specification lists `secp256k1` for ECGenParameterSpec, but the detector rule's finite list omits it.

Construction using another standardized ECGenParameterSpec name omitted by the rule, such as a documented `sect*`, `secp160*`, `secp192*`, or `secp224k1` name, when the selected provider supports that name.
Construction using a provider-documented predefined name or alias omitted by the rule, when evidence establishes provider support and the deployment's policy permits it.
protocol: Con := c1; ORDER Con, where c1 is ECGenParameterSpec(stdName).
